title: Is Social Media Ruining the Joy of Travel
paragraphs: Before traveling to a new place, many people now spend hours watching videos and looking at photos online. While this can help them plan their trips, some experts warn that it may also be taking away some of the excitement and surprise of travel.

According to a survey by the Hint App, which questioned 10,684 adults in Europe, the UK, the US, Canada, Australia and Latin America, 74% of tourists said they research destinations so thoroughly that few genuine surprises remain once they arrive. Moreover, 68% said that places they had never visited before already felt familiar because they had seen so much content about them online, and 64% said they recognized landmarks and viewpoints from social media.

Kirill Liakh, the managing director of Hint, explained that people use information to reduce uncertainty before an experience. Although this can make traveling easier, he said, it can also make the first encounter with a place feel less special.

Social media can also put pressure on travelers. In a study by the travel company TUI Musement, 37% of travelers said they felt pressure to make their trips look exciting on social media, rising to 45% among Gen Z. In addition, a survey by Forbes Advisor found that 42% of people had spent more than they planned, or gone into credit card debt, after seeing a similar trip on social media.

Nevertheless, social media may not be as powerful as people think. According to a survey carried out by the travel company Omio with YouGov in April 2026, only 6% of American travelers choose where to go because of social media trends or influencers.

So how can travelers keep some surprise in their trips? Some experts recommend using printed guidebooks, which cannot show every sight in detail. Travelers can also ask hotel staff or visit tourist information centers for local recommendations. Finally, simply walking around without a plan can be one of the best ways to discover unexpected cafes, restaurants and museums.
